QuestionStmt.S: Calculate the number of unit cells present in 1 g metal if the product of the density of metal and the volume of unit cell is $2.5 \times 10^{-22} \, \text{g}$.

Solution.S:
Step 1: The product of density of metal and volume of unit cell gives the mass of one unit cell.

Mass of one unit cell = $2.5 \times 10^{-22}$ g.

Step 2: Number of unit cells present in 1 g of metal is given by:

$$\text{Number of unit cells} = \frac{\text{Total mass}}{\text{Mass of one unit cell}}$$

$$= \frac{1}{2.5 \times 10^{-22}}$$

$$= \frac{1}{2.5} \times 10^{22}$$

$$= 0.4 \times 10^{22}$$

$$= 4.0 \times 10^{21}$$

Step 3: Therefore, the number of unit cells present in 1 g metal is $4.0 \times 10^{21}$.

Final Answer: $$\boxed{4.0 \times 10^{21}}$$

Hence, the correct option is D.
